topSignals.title: Bloom Energy CEO: "Visibility for 25 GW of Deployments" — Scandium Supply Chain Controversy Erupts
topSignals.text: — On the Q2 2026 earnings call (July 28), CEO K.R. Sridhar stated: "We have visibility currently based on what we are working for 25 gigawatts of like deployments. And we are not dependent on China." Scandium oxide — a trace dopant in every Bloom SOFC — is sourced from the waste streams of Ti/Ni/Co/bauxite/U processing across multiple countries, not dedicated mining; management claims this supply chain can support 25 GW/yr of annual production. A short-seller report subsequently surfaced, alleging that 25 GW/yr would require ~220 tonnes ScOx at the 5 GW milestone alone against a global 2030 projected supply of ~240 tonnes — triggering a ~12% stock drop from the August 12 record close ($391). Bloom rebutted; stock rebounded ~6%. At ~$700–800M revenue/GW, 25 GW implies a ~$17.5–20B cumulative product revenue opportunity, before the $25B Brookfield EaaS framework and service income. This is the most important scale signal for SOFC LCOE cost-curve modelling. Motley Fool / Yahoo Finance | Bloom ScOx blog | Discovery Alert — short-seller analysis | FuelCell China — rebound report

topSignals.title: PUCT August 20 Hearing — Tomorrow: ERCOT Batch Zero Scope, Good Cause Exception, Carve-Out Language
topSignals.text: — The PUCT open meeting tomorrow will set the formal scope, timeline, and interim interconnection rules for the suspended ERCOT Batch Zero Large Load process (~250–300 projects, 474 GW, 90% data centers). Pre-confirmed: truly islanded self-supply (no grid connection) falls outside ERCOT's process entirely. Key pending decisions: (a) "good cause" exception mechanism for individual projects; (b) whether the islanded carve-out is formalized in tariff language or remains informal guidance; (c) audit methodology and timeline. Outcome directly affects Hedgehog USA (1.5 GW Bloom SOFC Texas, 104 MW Phase 1 pre-construction) and sets the US self-supply precedent. Gibson Dunn | B&W Energy Law | ERCOT Batch Zero release

topSignals.title: Nature Nanotechnology PEM Catalyst Breakthrough: 75% Less Platinum, 85% Retention After 150,000 Cycles
topSignals.text: — WashU McKelvey School of Engineering (lead: Prof. Gang Wu; co-authors from Brookhaven NL, Lawrence Berkeley NL, Northeastern U, U Pittsburgh) published August 6 in Nature Nanotechnology: Pt-Co intermetallic nanoparticles heated to 1,000°C form a highly ordered structure that retains 85% of performance after 150,000 voltage cycles (~25,000h). 75% less platinum vs. conventional PEM catalysts. This directly addresses the primary barrier — cost and durability limits — that has kept PEM fuel cells out of mainstream data center deployment. If commercialised at scale, it represents a competing on-site power pathway to SOFC for AI data centers with green hydrogen access. SOFC remains differentiated by multi-fuel flexibility and higher electrical efficiency. phys.org | ScienceDaily | Intelligent Living

items.text: Elcogen (priority): Quiet day August 19. No new announcements. Status unchanged: E3000 G2 platform (>75% FC electrical efficiency, 90% with heat recovery, 650°C operating temperature) in volume production at ELCO I Tallinn (360 MW/yr); deliveries to key partners ongoing since Q2 2026. Most recent external activities in 2026: JNK India MoU (April 7), Bonicorn/Eltronic PtX Thailand partnership (March 23), EC Executive VP Teresa Ribera factory visit (June 2026). No new product or partnership announcements in August 2026. Elcogen newsroom

Topsoe (priority): Quiet day August 19. Status unchanged: Herning SOEC factory (500 MW/yr) hibernated pending H2 demand recovery; SOEC commercialisation shifted from project supply to technology licensing (First Ammonia ammonia-synthesis licensing deal, August 12 — not SOEC); CEO Elena Scaltritti since June 1, 2026; FY2026 guidance DKK 7,600–8,400M. No SOFC announcements; data-center commercial pathway deferred to 2029+. Topsoe.com
Other players: Quiet day August 19. No new announcements from Bloom Energy (25 GW disclosure was from July 28 Q2 call), FuelCell Energy, Ceres Power, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, or Aisin.

Bloom Energy 25 GW scale visibility (first full digest coverage): See Top Signal #1. At current ~$700–800M revenue/GW and 5 GW/yr manufacturing capacity, 25 GW represents a decade-scale opportunity. Scandium supply chain controversy is the key risk — short-seller claims near-term supply ceiling at ~5 GW/yr; Bloom management disputes this. LCOE cost-curve assumptions for post-2028 scenarios should be sensitivity-tested against both views.

Active pipeline carry-forward unchanged: Oracle Jupiter 2.45 GW (NMED September 14 hearing, gas supply unresolved); Crusoe/Cheyenne 900 MW Phase 1 (first data halls H2 2026); Hedgehog Texas 1.5 GW, 104 MW Phase 1 (PUCT August 20 — carve-out pending); Nebius/Bloom 328 MW Vineland NJ (confirmed active); FCEL/Fit Energy 380 MW (30 MW H2 2026); Equinix 100 MW+ (19+ DCs); Bloom/Brookfield $25B EaaS; ECL/PowerCell 300 MW+ H2-ready.

FERC RM26-4 — Comment period now open (~30 days, through ~September 16): All six RTOs/ISOs (PJM, MISO, NYISO, SPP, CAISO, ISO-NE) submitted responses to the FERC June 18 show cause orders by the August 17 deadline. Interested parties now have 30 days to comment on whether the filed tariff proposals are just and reasonable. Priority extracts: (a) PJM BYOG expedited track cost parameters; (b) MISO large-load study timeline and cost allocation; (c) NYISO self-supply treatment. These will replace the $5–20/MWh avoided-T-cost placeholder in the SOFC LCOE model. FERC RM26-4 docket | Climate Solutions Legal Digest — RTO preview

items.text: PUCT August 20 — Tomorrow (see Top Signal #2): Monitor for the formal "good cause" exception mechanism and cost-allocation language that will define behind-the-meter SOFC project economics in Texas.

Background unchanged: NY EO 62 data center moratorium (50 MW+, islanded exemption active); Germany EnEfG PUE ≤1.2/ERF ≥10%/15% waste heat from July 2026; ITC 48E 30% credit active for all fuel cell feedstocks.

Rolls-Royce SMR GDA Step 3 — August deadline virtually gone: As of August 19, ONR has not issued a Design Acceptance Confirmation (DAC). Approximately 6 working days remain in August; the 53-month GDA schedule targeting August 2026 completion appears to have slipped to Q4 2026. Confirmed slip would be the last working-days-of-August milestone to watch. Near-term impact: SOFC deployment speed advantage in UK/EU markets is maintained or extended. ONR GDA page

PEM fuel cell cost breakthrough (Nature Nanotechnology, Aug 6): See Top Signal #3. Pt-Co intermetallic nanoparticle approach reduces Pt loading by 75%, extends cycle life to 150,000 cycles. If it reaches production cost parity, PEM + H2 supply could compete with SOFC in green-hydrogen-accessible data center markets. SOFC differentiators — multi-fuel flexibility, higher electrical efficiency — remain intact in the near term.
Background unchanged: 13 hyperscaler nuclear deals >9.8 GW; nuclear 10+ year lead times; battery LCOE ~$25/MWh unsuitable for 24/7 AI baseload.

Bloom Energy (BE): A short-seller report alleging China dependency and physical impossibility of scaling ScOx supply to 25 GW wiped ~12% from the stock's August 12 record close ($391); Bloom's rebuttal (diversified non-China supply, waste-stream sourcing, Q2 earnings disclosures) drove a ~6% rebound. Stock trading around $244–246, ~+150% YTD vs. peak +435%. Valuation: ~$70B market cap, ~81× forward earnings (Motley Fool, August 16) — considered stretched but defensible if 25 GW pipeline converts. Bloom did NOT appear on Motley Fool's "10 best stocks to buy now" list. Near-term catalysts: PUCT August 20, NMED September 14, Bloom 10-Q (September 11), Q3 earnings (October). Motley Fool Aug 16 | 247wallst Aug 14

Broader markets (pre-open futures, Aug 19): S&P Futures −0.45%, Nasdaq Futures −0.89%, VIX +6.60% to 15.19; crude oil +0.99% to $85.34/bbl. Modest risk-off environment; crude price uptick increases gas-price sensitivity of SOFC LCOE.
FuelCell Energy (FCEL): No material new disclosures. Torrington 100 MW/yr target by October 31, 2026.
Ceres Power (CWR.L): No new corporate announcements. Next catalyst: H1 2026 results (September).

Nature Nanotechnology, August 6, 2026 (first appearance in digest): "Carbon nanostructure improves fuel-cell catalyst durability while reducing platinum use." WashU / Brookhaven NL / Lawrence Berkeley NL / Northeastern U / U Pittsburgh. Pt-Co intermetallic nanoparticles, ordered structure formed at 1,000°C, retained 85% performance after 150,000 voltage cycles (~25,000h). 75% less platinum vs. conventional PEM catalysts. Context: PEM technology milestone relevant as competing on-site power for H2-accessible data centers; not SOFC, but relevant for the competing-tech landscape and future hybrid SOFC/PEM scenarios. Not LCOE-model relevant for SOFC directly. phys.org | ScienceDaily

lcoe.text: Bloom scandium supply chain controversy (new, high priority): If the short-seller thesis is correct (~220t ScOx required at 5 GW milestone vs. ~240t global 2030 supply), Bloom faces a binding constraint above ~5 GW/yr — which caps the SOFC near-term cost-curve improvement rate. If management is correct (diversified waste-stream supply sufficient for 25 GW/yr), the cost curve can steepen materially post-2028. Sensitivity analysis needed: SOFC LCOE cost-curve shape under 5 GW/yr vs. 25 GW/yr production scenarios. Discovery Alert | Energies Media

FERC RM26-4 comment period (extract after ~September 16): Formal tariff text from each RTO/ISO is now public on FERC eLibrary. Priority extracts: (a) PJM BYOG track avoided-transmission-cost parameters; (b) MISO large-load study timeline; (c) NYISO self-supply cost allocation. These values replace the $5–20/MWh placeholder.

PUCT August 20 (tomorrow): Formal islanded carve-out language and any cost-allocation or registration requirements will affect behind-the-meter SOFC economics in Texas. Monitor for tariff filing post-meeting.

Natural gas / crude direction: Crude +0.99% to $85.34/bbl today. Watch EIA weekly gas storage report (Thursday August 20). SOFC LCOE sensitivity: +$1/MMBtu gas adds ~$10–15/MWh to LCOE at base case capex.

Background carry-forward unchanged: US natural gas $4.00–4.90/MMBtu (EIA 2026); SOFC commercial system capex $4,000–6,000/kW (target $1,000/kW); ITC 48E reduces effective capex to $2,800–4,200/kW; CCGT $2,000–2,200/kW; solar+battery $25/MWh LCOE (24/7 baseload-unsuitable).

(3) NMED September 14 — Project Jupiter air permit hearing. (4) Bloom 10-Q MW-shipped extraction (SEC EDGAR, due September 11). (5) Bloom scandium controversy resolution. (6) Elcogen E3000 G2 system-level efficiency confirmation at ELCO I production scale. (7) Ceres H1 2026 results (September). (8) Bloom Q3 2026 earnings (October). (9) Rolls-Royce SMR GDA Step 3 DAC from ONR (August deadline slipping to Q4).
